prompt.es: Redacta el calendario de apertura: dos futuros, dos encargos (have/get) y un plazo.

answer.text: Here is the timeline for opening the workshop. By the end of March, we will have signed the lease. Meanwhile, Leo is having the sign made by a carpenter, and we are getting the permit approved by the council. It should be ready by the fifteenth of April. In the middle of May, we will be putting up the shelves and painting the walls, and Sara will be building the website. Leo will delegate the accounts to Sara, so he can focus on the tools and the first customers. By the first of June, we will have opened the doors. The first milestone is to repair fifty bikes in the first month, and we will review the plan together in July.

This is our timeline. By the end of March, we will have signed the lease, and we are having the sign made by a carpenter. This week we are getting the permit approved by the council. In the middle of May, we will be painting the walls and putting up the shelves, while Sara will be working on the website. By the first of June, we will have opened the workshop. Our milestone is to repair fifty bikes in the first month, and Leo will delegate the accounts to Sara, so that he can look after the tools and the first customers. We will review the plan together in July, and then we will decide whether we are ready to hire a second mechanic.

feedback.es: Un calendario completo combina plazos con will have, acciones en curso con will be + -ing y encargos con have/get + participio.

title.en: Present the plan for a small business
title.es: Presentar el plan de un pequeño negocio

es: Presentar un plan de arranque para un negocio propio: calendario con plazos, tareas delegadas, un riesgo con su contingencia y respuesta a una objeción.

teaching.en: Thank you for coming. I will begin my pitch with the timeline.
teaching.es: Gracias por venir. Empezaré mi presentación con el calendario.
teaching.explanationEs: Una buena apertura saluda y dice qué vas a mostrar; pitch es la presentación breve de un proyecto.
segments: Thank you for coming. I will
begin my pitch with the timeline.
teaching.audioText: Thank you for coming. I will begin my pitch with the timeline.

teaching.en: Our forecast is fifty repairs a month by the end of the year.
teaching.es: Nuestra previsión es de cincuenta reparaciones al mes a finales de año.
teaching.explanationEs: Forecast es una previsión con cifras; se apoya en un plazo con by.
segments: Our forecast is fifty repairs a month
by the end of the year.
teaching.audioText: Our forecast is fifty repairs a month by the end of the year.

teaching.en: An investor may raise the objection that cycling drops in winter.
teaching.es: Un inversor puede plantear la objeción de que el ciclismo baja en invierno.
teaching.explanationEs: Objection es un reparo que alguien pone a tu plan; raise an objection = plantearlo.
segments: An investor may raise the objection
that cycling drops in winter.
teaching.audioText: An investor may raise the objection that cycling drops in winter.

teaching.en: I understand that concern, but let me reassure you: we have a contingency plan.
teaching.es: Entiendo esa preocupación, pero permítame tranquilizarle: tenemos un plan de contingencia.
teaching.explanationEs: Reconoce la preocupación antes de responder; reassure es transitivo, sin preposición.
segments: I understand that concern, but let me
reassure you: we have a contingency plan.
teaching.audioText: I understand that concern, but let me reassure you: we have a contingency plan.

teaching.en: Should demand fall, we will use our reserve, so we think the plan is realistic.
teaching.es: Si la demanda bajara, usaremos nuestra reserva, así que creemos que el plan es realista.
teaching.explanationEs: Realistic muestra que lo prometido se puede cumplir; la contingencia lo respalda.
segments: Should demand fall, we will use our reserve,
so we think the plan is realistic.
teaching.audioText: Should demand fall, we will use our reserve, so we think the plan is realistic.

teaching.en: I would like to address your objection briefly.
teaching.es: Me gustaría responder brevemente a su objeción.
teaching.explanationEs: Address significa abordar un reparo de manera directa; I would like to es cortés y formal.
segments: I would like to
address your objection briefly.
teaching.audioText: I would like to address your objection briefly.

prompt.es: Completa: «Permítame tranquilizarle: tenemos un plan de contingencia.»

answer.text: reassure

feedback.es: Reassure + persona es la fórmula para tranquilizar a quien ha planteado una duda.

hint.es: Es el verbo que significa tranquilizar.

origin.text: Let me ___ you: we have a contingency plan.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase reconoce la objeción y después responde?

choices.text: Your concern is wrong, so please stop asking.
I understand that concern, but our forecast is realistic.

feedback.es: La respuesta profesional reconoce el reparo y lo contesta con un dato; las otras lo rechazan o tienen un error de gramática.

hint.es: Busca la que primero reconoce y luego responde.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Empezaré con el calendario y la previsión.»

feedback.es: Reconoce la preocupación y responde con un dato concreto; las otras descalifican o no responden.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace el hablante ante la objeción.

feedback.es: Address y reassure indican que responde al reparo y tranquiliza.

prompt.es: Presenta el plan: calendario, encargos, un riesgo y respuesta a la objeción.

answer.text: Thank you for coming. I will begin my pitch with the timeline. By the end of March, we will have signed the lease, and we are getting the permit approved. Meanwhile, Leo is having the sign made, and this time next month we will be putting up the shelves. By the first of June, we will have opened the doors. The main risk is a fall in demand in winter. Should demand fall, we will use our cash reserve and offer home repairs. I understand your concern about the forecast, but let me reassure you: fifty repairs a month is realistic because two competitors are already busy and there is a niche for fast repairs.
